documented_fact: TxDOT-funded study evaluated PLCs with limestone content greater than 15%, including full-scale cement production and laboratory/outdoor exposure testing.
source_title: Laboratory and Outdoor Exposure Site Evaluations of Portland Limestone Cements
interpretation_limit: Research on >15% limestone cannot be treated as proof of Type IL acceptance or its motivation.

documented_fact: GDOT-sponsored assessment examined limestone blended cements for transportation applications, including performance and durability.
source_title: Assessment of Limestone Blended Cements for Transportation Applications
interpretation_limit: Study existence is not proof that its results caused a specification change.

documented_fact: IDOT-associated research evaluated concrete mixes with conventional and modified limestone cement contents for pavements and bridge decks.
source_title: Effect of Portland Cement with Limestone and Process Addition on the Performance of Concrete for Pavement and Bridge Decks
interpretation_limit: Modified ASTM C150 cement should not be conflated with ASTM C595 Type IL.

documented_fact: IDOT Type IL special provision effective August 1, 2023 adds Type IL to specified construction material applications.
source_title: Cement, Type IL (BDE), effective August 1, 2023
interpretation_limit: Shows specification permission in cited applications, not measured usage or reasons for the change.

documented_fact: FDOT 2022 proposed specification lists Type IL among permitted cement types and specifies separate storage and heat-of-hydration reporting.
source_title: Section 921 Portland Cement and Blended Cement, revision July 29, 2022
interpretation_limit: Review/draft document: do not infer final implementation or decision rationale.

documented_fact: Louisiana DOTD May 2022 testing requirements specify Type IL conformity with AASHTO M 240 and alkali testing for cement types.
source_title: Portland Cement and Blended Hydraulic Cement, May 2022
interpretation_limit: Testing requirements are not evidence of the historical reason for acceptance.

documented_fact: FHWA published a PLC TechNote covering specifications, sustainability, performance, case studies and implementation best practices for state highway agencies.
source_title: Portland Limestone Cement, FHWA-HRT-23-104
interpretation_limit: Federal guidance is not an individual state DOT adoption decision.

documented_fact: PCA announced that 44 state DOTs accepted PLC after recent approvals in Maryland, Arizona and Vermont.
source_title: A Milestone for Sustainable Infrastructure — 44 State DOTs Now Accept PLC
interpretation_limit: Secondary industry announcement; acceptance dates and specific conditions require DOT confirmation.

documented_fact: May 21 2020 scoping document states Type IL was not then permitted by Caltrans specifications and industry partners requested consideration; task group sought to assess performance and avoid delaying Type IL milestones.
source_title: Impact of Portland Limestone Cement (PLC) on Concrete Performance — Work Product Scoping Document
interpretation_limit: Documents discussion and research scope, not an adoption decision or measured performance.

documented_fact: October 15 2021 directive allows ASTM C595/AASHTO M240 Type IL under revised specification; cites sustainability, reduced greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption while maintaining equivalent quality/performance.
source_title: CPD 21-19 Portland-Limestone Cement Allowance in Blended Cements
interpretation_limit: Explicit stated policy rationale; does not isolate which consideration was decisive.

documented_fact: For projects advertised before October 15 2021 or lacking revised specifications, contractors could request Type IL use through a no-cost change order requiring resident-engineer approval.
source_title: CPD 21-19 Portland-Limestone Cement Allowance in Blended Cements
interpretation_limit: Procedure for legacy contracts; not a count of actual approvals or projects.

documented_fact: December 22 2021 memo describes cement industry switching to Type IL to reduce emissions and sets requirements for acceptance and trial batching.
source_title: Type IL Cement Mix Design Acceptance and Trial Batching
interpretation_limit: Memo describes industry context, not direct evidence that a particular manufacturer caused a DOT decision.

documented_fact: WisDOT requires full mix-design submittal and trial batching for specified Class I scenarios; for specified Class II scenarios trial batching is not required; material certification, approved-source listing and sample submission also required.
source_title: Type IL Cement Mix Design Acceptance and Trial Batching
interpretation_limit: Requirements vary by concrete class and contract status; do not generalize to all Wisconsin projects.

documented_fact: GDOT-sponsored comparison of five cement producers’ Type IL and Type I/II materials found tested Type IL concretes satisfied the evaluated GDOT concrete-class specifications; interplant differences in mechanical properties generally exceeded within-plant differences between cement types.
source_title: Assessment of Limestone Blended Cements for Transportation Applications
interpretation_limit: Laboratory findings for evaluated cements and mix classes; not direct proof of a later DOT approval decision.

documented_fact: TxDOT project 0-6858 began January 16 2015 to investigate PLC containing more than 15% limestone; stated aim was to identify implementation obstacles and evaluate fresh, hardened and durability properties.
source_title: Evaluating Limestone Cements Containing Greater Than 15% Limestone — Project 0-6858
interpretation_limit: Research concerns >15% limestone and cannot be treated as evidence against ordinary ASTM Type IL (up to 15%).

documented_fact: CDOT permitted ASTM C1157 portland-limestone cement containing up to 10% limestone for a U.S. Highway 287 pavement project near Lamar, constructed 2008–2009; the mixture included 20% Class F fly ash.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (CP Road Map Brief, October 2018)
interpretation_limit: Retrospective technical brief, not the original 2008 approval memorandum. ASTM C1157 GU PLC is not identical to the later ASTM C595 Type IL designation; project permission is not statewide Type IL acceptance.

documented_fact: A 2018 technical brief reports CDOT viewed PLC use as supporting Colorado climate goals; its U.S. 287 project reported average 28-day flexural strength of 695 psi against a 650 psi requirement.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (CP Road Map Brief, October 2018)
interpretation_limit: Reported project result and retrospective statement, not an independently measured effect of PLC on performance or proof of the sole motivation for approval. Shares source and project with 2008 row.

documented_fact: A contemporary industry case study reports Utah DOT had long accepted ASTM C1157 cements and permitted addition of fly ash to ASTM C1157 cement at concrete batch plants in 2008; Lost Creek Road used ASTM C1157 GU PLC with 20% Class F fly ash.
source_title: Performance-enhancing (Roads & Bridges, 2010)
interpretation_limit: Industry account, not a UDOT specification or decision memorandum. Pre-existing acceptance of ASTM C1157 and 2008 fly-ash permission must not be relabeled as first acceptance of ASTM C595 Type IL.

documented_fact: An INDOT-sponsored study compared PLC containing up to 15% limestone with OPC; it found broadly similar mechanical properties and stated INDOT could consider ASTM C595/AASHTO M240 PLC suitable for concrete applications.
source_title: Performance of Portland Limestone Cements (FHWA/IN/JTRP-2013/29)
interpretation_limit: Research recommendation, not a dated specification adoption or proof INDOT implemented the recommendation; reported material-specific performance should not be generalized to all sources.

documented_fact: ODOT I-40 Crosstown Expressway reconstruction used a cement described as Type IL(10) with 10% limestone; the project began in 2009 and was scheduled for completion in 2012.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: The 2018 account documents project use, not the original ODOT approval date or agency-wide Type IL acceptance.

documented_fact: ODOT structural materials engineer Matt Romero reported satisfactory workability and placement on PLC paving projects and no known subsequent field issues.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: Retrospective agency staff testimony; no quantitative long-term comparative performance estimate.

documented_fact: The 2018 MAP Brief reported the material was addressed in ODOT concrete paving specifications through a special provision and that incorporation into the next specification book was expected.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: The exact special provision and formal approval date were not independently located; the brief inconsistently labels Type IL as Type II in this passage.

documented_fact: UDOT ran a PLC trial in the Salt Lake Valley in 2009; the 2018 account reports an evaluation comparing PLC and OPC properties and subsequent use on SR 201.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: Trial described retrospectively; does not establish first state-wide Type IL approval.

documented_fact: On SR 201, eastbound lanes used OPC with 25% Class F fly ash in August 2009; westbound lanes used PLC with 10% interground limestone and 25% Class F fly ash in October 2009, about 6,000 tons of PLC.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: Different placement dates and conditions mean this is not a controlled experiment establishing causal equivalence.

documented_fact: Denver 40th Avenue and Havana construction projects used ASTM C1157 Type GU PLC with 20% fly ash and recycled concrete aggregates in 2007.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: City/developer project, not evidence of formal CDOT acceptance in 2007.

documented_fact: The 2018 MAP Brief describes limited PLC sales under ASTM C1157 during 2005–2012 and addition of Type IL to ASTM C595 and AASHTO M240 in 2012.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cement after 10 Years in the Field (October 2018)
interpretation_limit: National standards milestone, not a state DOT approval decision; overlaps historical context in Module 03.

documented_fact: UDOT reported that portland cement shortages were causing project budget and schedule problems. It expedited PLC materials testing, found comparable workability, performance and long-term durability, and approved the alternative to increase concrete supply.
source_title: UDOT 2023 Innovation and Efficiencies Report — Crushed Limestone Cement Helps Alleviate Supply Chain Shortages
interpretation_limit: 2023 retrospective account of a later supply-chain response; not evidence of the rationale for UDOT’s 2009 SR 201 project or original Type IL acceptance date.

evidence_type: TRB technical presentation documenting 2009 field comparison
documented_fact: A TRB-hosted technical presentation describes the 2009 SR 201 comparison: eastbound lanes paved August 2009 with ASTM C150 Type II/V cement; westbound lanes paved October 2009 with ASTM C1157 cement containing 10% limestone. Both mixes included 25% Class F fly ash.
source_title: Portland-Limestone Cements: History, Performance, and Specifications — TRB webinar presentation
interpretation_limit: Technical presentation, not original UDOT authorization or trial report; different placement dates and temperatures prevent controlled causal comparison. Source publication period should be checked before precise dating.
